title: Amidst a World of Hopes and Fears
description: Amidst a World of Hopes and Fears in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Moore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 487 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Religious Principle”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-midst a world of hopes and fears, A wild of cares, and toils, and tears, Where foes a-larm and dan-gers threat, And plea-sures kill, and glo-ries cheat:

lines: Amidst a world of hopes and fears,
A wild of cares, and toils, and tears,
Where foes alarm and dangers threat,
And pleasures kill, and glories cheat:
Shed down, O Lord! a heavenly ray,
To guide me in the doubtful way;
And o'er me hold thy shield of power,
To guard me in the dangerous hour.
Teach me the flattering paths to shun,
In which the thoughtless many run,
Who for a shade the substance miss,
And grasp their ruin in their bliss.
May never pleasure, wealth or pride,
But through this maze of mortal ill,
Safe lead me to thy heavenly hill.

licence: Public domain: Henry Moore died in 1802.
credits: Words by Henry Moore (1732–1802), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
